Authentication

Every request to the Acme API must be authenticated. The API accepts two credential types: a bearer token for server-side calls, and a signed request for calls made from an untrusted client where a long-lived secret cannot be stored.

Bearer tokens

Send your secret key in the Authorization header. Secret keys are scoped to a single project and never expire, so treat one exactly as you would a password: keep it out of version control and rotate it if it is ever exposed.

curl https://api.acme.com/v1/websites \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_SECRET_KEY"

Signed requests

When a request originates from a browser or a mobile client, sign it on your own server instead of shipping a secret key to the device. A signature is valid for five minutes from the timestamp it carries, which bounds how long a captured request can be replayed.

  1. Build the canonical string from the method, the path, and the request body.
  2. Sign it with your project secret using HMAC-SHA256.
  3. Send the result in the X-Acme-Signature header alongside the timestamp.

Requests that fail verification return 401. See errors and retries for the full list of authentication failure codes and whether each one is safe to retry.
